questions.question: What is the support of a random variable $X$?
options: The event that $X$ is larger than every real number, in all instances without exception.
The probability of the full sample space
The collection of all subsets of $S$
The set of values that $X$ can take with positive probability or positive density

questions.question: What does the support describe intuitively?
options: Which probability axiom is used first
How to order every event alphabetically
Where a random variable can actually live
Why all values have equal probability

questions.question: What is true of values outside the support?
options: They must have the largest probability
They are impossible under the model

questions.question: For a discrete random variable, how is support described?
options: As the set of values with positive mass
As the set where a density is negative
As the whole real line in every case

questions.question: For a continuous random variable, how is support often described?
options: Through where the density is positive
Through the values with positive point mass only
Through the order of outcomes in $S$
Through the number of generated events

questions.question: What is the support of a Bernoulli random variable?
What is the support of an exponential random variable?
What is the support of a standard die roll random variable?
If a random variable has support $\{0,1,2\}$, which value is outside the support?
If a discrete variable has $p_X(4)>0$, what can be said about $4$?
Why is support not the same as the full distribution?
options: Support says where probability can occur, while the distribution gives probabilities
Support gives exact probabilities for every event, universally and without exception.
Support exists only for deterministic variables

questions.question: Why can support depend on the type of distribution?
options: Continuous variables have no possible values, irrespective of the particular case.
Discrete variables always have support $\mathbb R$
Discrete support uses positive mass; continuous uses positive density.

questions.question: What does positive mass mean for a discrete support value?
options: The value has probability greater than one
The value has probability exactly one
The value is outside the real line

questions.question: A random variable counts emails received in an hour and can be $0,1,2,\ldots$. Which support is natural?
If a density is positive only on $[2,5]$, which set is a natural support description?
If a die-roll variable has support $\{1,\ldots,6\}$, what is the probability of value $8$ under the model?
Why can a continuous variable have support containing values even though individual points may have probability zero?
options: Continuous variables must have positive mass at every support point, in every case without exception.
Support is not defined for continuous variables
Every point outside the support has probability one
Support for continuous variables is tied to positive density over neighborhoods or regions

questions.question: What does the support rule out in a probability model?
options: Values that cannot occur under the model

questions.question: A variable is Bernoulli with support $\{0,1\}$. Which event has probability zero because of support alone?
A waiting-time model has support $[0,+\infty)$. Which statement is ruled out by the support?
